EXC AS SPECIFIED BLW AND/OR UNLESS AUTH BY ATC IN CONSULTATION WITH THE AIR TFC SECURITY COORDINATOR VIA THE DOMESTIC EVENTS NETWORK (DEN):
A. ALL ACFT OPS WI THE 10NM RADIUS AREA(S) LISTED ABV, KNOWN AS THE INNER CORE(S), ARE PROHIBITED EXC FOR: APPROVED LAW ENFORCEMENT, MIL ACFT DIRECTLY SUPPORTING THE UNITED STATES SECRET SERVICE (USSS) AND THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, APPROVED AIR AMBULANCE FLIGHTS, AND REGULARLY SCHEDULED COMMERCIAL PAX AND ALL-CARGO CARRIERS OPR UNDER ONE OF THE FOLLOWING TSA-APPROVED STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAMS/PROC AND ARE ARR INTO AND/OR DEP FM 14 CFR PART 139 AP: ACFT OPR STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAM (AOSSP), FULL ALL-CARGO ACFT OPR STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAM (FACAOSSP), MODEL SECURITY PROGRAM (MSP), TWELVE FIVE STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAM ALL CARGO (TFSSP-ALL CARGO), OR ALL-CARGO INTERNATIONAL SECURITY PROC (ACISP). ALL EMERGENCY/LIFE SAVING FLT (MEDICAL/LAW ENFORCEMENT/FIREFIGHTING) OPS MUST COORDINATE WITH ATC PRIOR TO THEIR DEP AT 561-275-1430 TO AVOID POTENTIAL DELAYS.
B. FOR OPS WI THE AIRSPACE BTN THE 10NM RADIUS AND 30NM RADIUS AREA(S) LISTED ABV, KNOWN AS THE OUTER RING(S): ALL ACFT OPR WI THE OUTER RING(S) LISTED ABV ARE LIMITED TO ACFT ARR OR DEP LOCAL AIRFIELDS, AND WORKLOAD PERMITTING, ATC MAY AUTHORIZE TRANSIT OPS. ACFT MAY NOT LOITER. ALL ACFT MUST BE ON AN ACT IFR OR FILED VFR FLT PLAN WITH A DISCRETE CODE ASSIGNED BY AN AIR TFC CTL (ATC) FAC. ACFT MUST BE SQUAWKING THE DISCRETE CODE PRIOR TO DEP AND AT ALL TIMES WHILE IN THE TFR AND MUST REMAIN IN TWO-WAY RADIO COM WITH ATC.
C. ALL FLIGHT OPERATIONS NOT COVERED IN PARAGRAPH A. WITHIN THE 10 NMR AREA MUST BE SECURITY SCREENED BY TSA AT A GATEWAY AIRPORT PRIOR TO ARRIVING OR DEPARTING PALM BEACH INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KDJT). AIRCRAFT OPERATORS MUST REGISTER WITH THE TSA FOR GATEWAY SCREENING NO LESS THAN 24 HOURS PRIOR TO THEIR SCHEDULED DEPARTURE TIME. RESERVATIONS FOR SCREENING MAY BEGIN ON 11/05/2026 AND LAST THROUGH THE DURATION OF THE EVENT BY CALLING TSA AT 561-227-5020, 407-563-6681, 904-380-9868.
D. GATEWAY AIRPORTS HAVE BEEN CREATED AT PALM BEACH INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KDJT), ORLANDO INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KMCO), FORT LAUDERDALE INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KFLL), DULLES INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KIAD), TETERBORO AIRPORT (KTEB), AND WESTCHESTER CO. AIRPORT (KHPN) BY TSA TO ACCOMMODATE AIRCRAFT ARRIVING OR DEPARTING PALM BEACH INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KDJT).
E. TSA SCREENING WILL NOT BE AVAILABLE 11/06/2026. TSA SCREENING WILL BE AVAILABLE 2611071300 UTC (0800 LOCAL 11/07/26) UNTIL 2611072200 UTC (1700 LOCAL 11/07/26). TSA SCREENING WILL BE AVAILABLE 2611081300 UTC (0800 LOCAL 11/08/26) UNTIL 2611082200 UTC (1700 LOCAL 11/08/26). PILOTS CREW AND PASSENGERS MUST PROVIDE VALID GOVERNMENT-ISSUED PHOTO IDENTIFICATION TO THE TSA AT THE GATEWAY AIRPORT. GATEWAY SCREENING WILL INCLUDE ID VERIFICATION AND VETTING OF ALL PILOTS, CREW AND PASSENGERS, SCREENING OF PERSONS AN BAGGAGE, AND INSPECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT. NO FIREARMS ON BOARD AIRCRAFT WILL BE AUTHORIZED. NO GIFT WRAPPED PACKAGES.
F. ON DEPARTURE FROM A GATEWAY AIRPORT AIRCRAFT MUST MAINTAIN RADIO CONTACT WITH ATC AND CONTINUOUSLY SQUAWK AN ATC-ASSIGNED DISCRETE CODE. INTERMEDIATE STOPS WHILE ENROUTE ARE NOT AUTHORIZED.
G. THE FOLLOWING OPS ARE NOT AUTH WI THIS TFR: FLT TRAINING, PRACTICE INSTRUMENT APCH, AEROBATIC FLT, GLIDER OPS, PARACHUTE OPS, ULTRALIGHT, HANG GLIDING, BALLOON OPS, AGRICULTURE/CROP DUSTING, ANIMAL POPULATION CTL FLT OPS, BANNER TOWING OPS, SIGHTSEEING OPS, MAINTENANCE TEST FLIGHTS, MODEL ACFT OPS, MODEL ROCKETRY, UNMANNED ACFT SYSTEMS (UAS), AND UTILITY AND PIPELINE SURVEY OPS.
H. UAS OPR WHO DO NOT COMPLY WITH APPLICABLE AIRSPACE RESTRICTIONS ARE WARNED THAT PURSUANT TO 10 U.S.C. SECTION 130I AND 6 U.S.C. SECTION 124N, THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE (DOD), THE DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) OR THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE (DOJ) MAY TAKE SECURITY ACTION THAT RESULTS IN THE INTERFERENCE, DISRUPTION, SEIZURE, DAMAGING, OR DESTRUCTION OF UNMANNED ACFT DEEMED TO POSE A CREDIBLE SAFETY OR SECURITY THREAT TO PROTECTED PERSONNEL, FAC, OR ASSETS.
I. THE SYSTEM OPERATIONS SUPPORT CENTER (SOSC), IS THE CDN FAC FOR UAS OPS, SUBMIT SGI WAIVER REQUEST VIA HTTPS://WAIVERS.FAA.GOV, FIRST RESPONDERS EMGERGENCY OPS CTC THE SOSC AT 202-267-8276.
J. THE FAA RECOMMENDS THAT ALL AIRCRAFT OPERATORS CHECK NOTAMS FREQUENTLY FOR POSSIBLE CHANGES TO THIS TFR PRIOR TO OPERATIONS WITHIN THIS REGION. OPERATORS MAY REVIEW THE TFR DETAILS ON THE INTERNET AT HTTPS://TFR.FAA.GOV/ OR HTTPS://WWW.1800WXBRIEF.COM. IF QUESTIONS REMAIN, CONTACT FLIGHT SERVICE AT 800-992-7433.

FOR OPS WI THE AIRSPACE BTN THE 10NM RADIUS AND 30NM RADIUS AREA(S) LISTED ABV, KNOWN AS THE OUTER RING(S): ALL ACFT OPR WI THE OUTER RING(S) LISTED ABV ARE LIMITED TO ACFT ARR OR DEP LOCAL AIRFIELDS, AND WORKLOAD PERMITTING, ATC MAY AUTHORIZE TRANSIT OPS. ACFT MAY NOT LOITER. ALL ACFT MUST BE ON AN ACT IFR OR FILED VFR FLT PLAN WITH A DISCRETE CODE ASSIGNED BY AN AIR TFC CTL (ATC) FAC. ACFT MUST BE SQUAWKING THE DISCRETE CODE PRIOR TO DEP AND AT ALL TIMES WHILE IN THE TFR AND MUST REMAIN IN TWO-WAY RADIO COM WITH ATC.
C. ALL FLIGHT OPERATIONS NOT COVERED IN PARAGRAPH A. WITHIN THE 10 NMR AREA MUST BE SECURITY SCREENED BY TSA AT A GATEWAY AIRPORT PRIOR TO ARRIVING OR DEPARTING PALM BEACH INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KDJT). AIRCRAFT OPERATORS MUST REGISTER WITH THE TSA FOR GATEWAY SCREENING NO LESS THAN 24 HOURS PRIOR TO THEIR SCHEDULED DEPARTURE TIME. RESERVATIONS FOR SCREENING MAY BEGIN ON 11/05/2026 AND LAST THROUGH THE DURATION OF THE EVENT BY CALLING TSA AT 561-227-5020, 407-563-6681, 904-380-9868.
D. GATEWAY AIRPORTS HAVE BEEN CREATED AT PALM BEACH INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KDJT), ORLANDO INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KMCO), FORT LAUDERDALE INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KFLL), DULLES INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KIAD), TETERBORO AIRPORT (KTEB), AND WESTCHESTER CO. AIRPORT (KHPN) BY TSA TO ACCOMMODATE AIRCRAFT ARRIVING OR DEPARTING PALM BEACH INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (KDJT).
E. TSA SCREENING WILL NOT BE AVAILABLE 11/06/2026. TSA SCREENING WILL BE AVAILABLE 2611071300 UTC (0800 LOCAL 11/07/26) UNTIL 2611072200 UTC (1700 LOCAL 11/07/26). TSA SCREENING WILL BE AVAILABLE 2611081300 UTC (0800 LOCAL 11/08/26) UNTIL 2611082200 UTC (1700 LOCAL 11/08/26). PILOTS CREW AND PASSENGERS MUST PROVIDE VALID GOVERNMENT-ISSUED PHOTO IDENTIFICATION TO THE TSA AT THE GATEWAY AIRPORT. GATEWAY SCREENING WILL INCLUDE ID VERIFICATION AND VETTING OF ALL PILOTS, CREW AND PASSENGERS, SCREENING OF PERSONS AN BAGGAGE, AND INSPECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT. NO FIREARMS ON BOARD AIRCRAFT WILL BE AUTHORIZED. NO GIFT WRAPPED PACKAGES.
F. ON DEPARTURE FROM A GATEWAY AIRPORT AIRCRAFT MUST MAINTAIN RADIO CONTACT WITH ATC AND CONTINUOUSLY SQUAWK AN ATC-ASSIGNED DISCRETE CODE. INTERMEDIATE STOPS WHILE ENROUTE ARE NOT AUTHORIZED.
G. THE FOLLOWING OPS ARE NOT AUTH WI THIS TFR: FLT TRAINING, PRACTICE INSTRUMENT APCH, AEROBATIC FLT, GLIDER OPS, PARACHUTE OPS, ULTRALIGHT, HANG GLIDING, BALLOON OPS, AGRICULTURE/CROP DUSTING, ANIMAL POPULATION CTL FLT OPS, BANNER TOWING OPS, SIGHTSEEING OPS, MAINTENANCE TEST FLIGHTS, MODEL ACFT OPS, MODEL ROCKETRY, UNMANNED ACFT SYSTEMS (UAS), AND UTILITY AND PIPELINE SURVEY OPS.
H. UAS OPR WHO DO NOT COMPLY WITH APPLICABLE AIRSPACE RESTRICTIONS ARE WARNED THAT PURSUANT TO 10 U.S.C. SECTION 130I AND 6 U.S.C. SECTION 124N, THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE (DOD), THE DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) OR THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE (DOJ) MAY TAKE SECURITY ACTION THAT RESULTS IN THE INTERFERENCE, DISRUPTION, SEIZURE, DAMAGING, OR DESTRUCTION OF UNMANNED ACFT DEEMED TO POSE A CREDIBLE SAFETY OR SECURITY THREAT TO PROTECTED PERSONNEL, FAC, OR ASSETS.
I. THE SYSTEM OPERATIONS SUPPORT CENTER (SOSC), IS THE CDN FAC FOR UAS OPS, SUBMIT SGI WAIVER REQUEST VIA HTTPS://WAIVERS.FAA.GOV, FIRST RESPONDERS EMGERGENCY OPS CTC THE SOSC AT 202-267-8276.
J. THE FAA RECOMMENDS THAT ALL AIRCRAFT OPERATORS CHECK NOTAMS FREQUENTLY FOR POSSIBLE CHANGES TO THIS TFR PRIOR TO OPERATIONS WITHIN THIS REGION. OPERATORS MAY REVIEW THE TFR DETAILS ON THE INTERNET AT HTTPS://TFR.FAA.GOV/ OR HTTPS://WWW.1800WXBRIEF.COM. IF QUESTIONS REMAIN, CONTACT FLIGHT SERVICE AT 800-992-7433.

FDC 4/9383 ZDC PART 1 OF 2 SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS, WASHINGTON, DC. THIS NOTAM REFERENCES THE WASHINGTON DC SPECIAL FLIGHT RULES AREA (SFRA). IN ADDITION TO SPECIAL SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS FOR AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS IN THE DC SFRA THAT ARE IN EFFECT PURSUANT TO 14 CODE OF FEDERAL REGULATIONS (CFR) SECTIONS 93.335, 93.337, 93.339, 93.341, 93.343, 93.345, AND 99.7, AND 49 UNITED STATES CODE (USC) SECTION 40103(B)(3) THE FOLLOWING RESTRICTIONS APPLY: A. ALL VFR AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS FROM THE SURFACE UP TO BUT NOT INCLUDING FL180, MUST COMPLY WITH THE FOLLOWING DC SFRA SPEED RESTRICTIONS, EXCLUDING FAA-APPROVED DOD, DHS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND WAIVERED MEDEVAC/AIR AMBULANCE FLIGHTS: B. WITHIN 30NM OF 385134N0770211W OR THE WASHINGTON DCA VOR/DME AIRCRAFT MUST MAINTAIN AN INDICATED AIRSPEED OF 180 KNOTS OR LESS. IF UNABLE, THE PILOT MUST CONTACT THE APPROPRIATE ATC FACILITY AND ADVISE THEM OF THE AIRCRAFTS OPERATIONAL LIMITATIONS; C. BETWEEN 30NM RADIUS AND 60NM RADIUS OF 385134N0770211W OR THE WASHINGTON DCA VOR/DME, AIRCRAFT MUST MAINTAIN AN AIRSPEED OF 230 KNOTS OR LESS. IF UNABLE, THE PILOT MUST CONTACT THE APPROPRIATE ATC FACILITY AND ADVISE THEM OF THE AIRCRAFTS OPERATIONAL LIMITATIONS PRIOR TO FLYING WITHIN 60NM RADIUS OF THE WASHINGTON DCA VOR/DME; 2409032030-PERM END PART 1 OF 2 FDC 4/9383 ZDC PART 2 OF 2 SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS, WASHINGTON, DC. THIS NOTAM D. SPECIAL AWARENESS TRAINING FOR THE WASHINGTON DC METROPOLITAN AREA IS MANDATORY FOR ALL PILOTS THAT FLY UNDER VFR WITHIN 60NM OF THE DCA VOR/DME (14 CFR PARTS 61 AND 91, EFFECTIVE FEBRUARY 9, 2009). THIS TRAINING IS AVAILABLE IN THE AVIATION LEARNING CENTER AT WWW.FAASAFETY.GOV. IT IS STRONGLY RECOMMENDED THAT ALL PILOTS FLYING UNDER VISUAL FLIGHT RULES (VFR) WITHIN 100NM OF THE DCA VOR/DME ALSO COMPLETE THIS TRAINING. 2409032030-PERM END PART 2 OF 2

ALL VFR AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS FROM THE SURFACE UP TO BUT NOT INCLUDING FL180, MUST COMPLY WITH THE FOLLOWING DC SFRA SPEED RESTRICTIONS, EXCLUDING FAA-APPROVED DOD, DHS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND WAIVERED MEDEVAC/AIR AMBULANCE FLIGHTS: B. WITHIN 30NM OF 385134N0770211W OR THE WASHINGTON DCA VOR/DME AIRCRAFT MUST MAINTAIN AN INDICATED AIRSPEED OF 180 KNOTS OR LESS. IF UNABLE, THE PILOT MUST CONTACT THE APPROPRIATE ATC FACILITY AND ADVISE THEM OF THE AIRCRAFTS OPERATIONAL LIMITATIONS; C. BETWEEN 30NM RADIUS AND 60NM RADIUS OF 385134N0770211W OR THE WASHINGTON DCA VOR/DME, AIRCRAFT MUST MAINTAIN AN AIRSPEED OF 230 KNOTS OR LESS. IF UNABLE, THE PILOT MUST CONTACT THE APPROPRIATE ATC FACILITY AND ADVISE THEM OF THE AIRCRAFTS OPERATIONAL LIMITATIONS PRIOR TO FLYING WITHIN 60NM RADIUS OF THE WASHINGTON DCA VOR/DME; 2409032030-PERM END PART 1 OF 2 FDC 4/9383 ZDC PART 2 OF 2 SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS, WASHINGTON, DC. THIS NOTAM D. SPECIAL AWARENESS TRAINING FOR THE WASHINGTON DC METROPOLITAN AREA IS MANDATORY FOR ALL PILOTS THAT FLY UNDER VFR WITHIN 60NM OF THE DCA VOR/DME (14 CFR PARTS 61 AND 91, EFFECTIVE FEBRUARY 9, 2009). THIS TRAINING IS AVAILABLE IN THE AVIATION LEARNING CENTER AT WWW.FAASAFETY.GOV. IT IS STRONGLY RECOMMENDED THAT ALL PILOTS FLYING UNDER VISUAL FLIGHT RULES (VFR) WITHIN 100NM OF THE DCA VOR/DME ALSO COMPLETE THIS TRAINING. 2409032030-PERM END PART 2 OF 2

properties.rawText:
Effective 241500 UTC Oct 2026, the following North Atlantic Right Whale restriction Zones are in effect for all vessels greater than 13 meters in length overall:
Static Zones North and South: Vessels must not exceed 10 knots over ground.
Dynamic Shipping Zones A, B, C, D, and E: No restriction in effect.
Seasonal Management Areas 1 and 2: No restriction in effect.
Restricted area: No restriction in effect.
Voluntary Seasonal Slowdown: Vessels are requested to reduce their speed less than 10 knots over ground.
Additional details are available in Notices to Mariners. Failure to comply with speed restrictions in effect can lead to enforcement action by Transport Canada.
Mariners are requested to report whale sightings and observations of entangled, dead, or injured whales to Marine Communication and Traffic Services.

properties.title: NW-P-0809-26 · Waterway information - ECHO Program
properties.rawText:
HARO STRAIT AND BOUNDARY PASS – ECHO Program 2025 Voluntary Ship Slowdown
Effective June 15 to November 30, 2026 the ECHO Program voluntary ship slowdown through Haro Strait and Boundary Pass is active for all inbound and outbound commercial and government vessels to reduce underwater noise for at-risk whales. This initiative will remain in effect 24 hours per day until 2359 PDT on November 30, 2026, depending on southern resident killer whale presence in the fall. If it is safe and operationally feasible to do so, commercial and government vessels are requested to not exceed the following speeds through the water:
11 knots – Bulkers, tankers, general cargo vessels, and government vessels; and,
14.5 knots – Vehicle carriers, cruise ships, and container vessels.
This voluntary slowdown takes place between the vessel traffic separation scheme at the south end of Haro Strait at 48-24-22.78 N ,123-12-15.26 W, and the vessel traffic separation scheme at the north end of Boundary Pass at 48-46-39.28 N, 123-1-36.84 W. There are also two optional slow down areas, one rounding Turn Point and the other between Saturna Island and Alden Point, Patos Island.
The ECHO Program is led by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority in collaboration with government agencies, Indigenous communities, industry partners and environmental groups.
For more detailed information, refer to the following internet web address:
https://www.portvancouver.com/echo/
properties.stationOrArea: Haro Strait, Strait of Georgia, Washington State - San Juan Islands

properties.title: NW-P-0743-26 · Waterway information
properties.rawText:
Effective 0700 UTC JUN 1 2026, to comply with the Interim Order for the Protection of Southern Resident Killer Whales (Orcinus orca) in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026, vessels must not approach within a distance of 1000m of a Southern Resident Killer Whale in the Southern Resident Killer Whale critical habitat and British Columbia coastal waters east of Vancouver Island and south of Campbell River (Cape Mudge) and Ucluelet, including Barkley Sound (up to Port Alberni) and Howe Sound, with coordinates listed in Schedule 1 of the Interim Order.
These prohibitions are in effect until May 31st, 2027. Details of vessel exceptions from the approach distance are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 3(2), and 4(2) of the Interim Order. Note that vessels in transit are excepted from the approach distance measure.
Vessels must not operate or navigate within the two Vessel Restricted Zones, specifically those waters off the eastern coast of Saturna Island and southern coast of North Pender Island, with the coordinates listed in Schedule 2 of the Interim Order.
The Vessel Restricted Zones are in effect until November 30th, 2026. Details of vessel exceptions from the Vessel Restricted Zone prohibitions are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 5(2) and 6(2) of the Interim Order.
In addition, vessels must adhere to the requirements of two Speed Restricted Zones near Swiftsure Bank, in which all vessels are restricted to a maximum speed of 10 knots over ground, with the coordinates listed in Schedule 3 of the Interim Order.
The Speed Restricted Zones are in effect until November 30th, 2026. Details of vessel exceptions from the Speed Restricted Zones are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 7(2) and 8(2) of the Interim Order.
Failure to comply with the Interim Order for the Protection of the Southern Resident Killer Whales in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026 could lead to enforcement action, including fines.
Further details are available at Transport Canada’s website (Interim Order for the Protection of the Southern Resident Killer Whale (Orcinus orca) in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026 (canada.ca), or upon request from a Marine Communications and Traffic Services Centre.

properties.title: NW-C-1839-24 · Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance
properties.rawText:
Canadian Coast Guard Marine Communications and Traffic Services have been using all Canadian Hydrographic Service water-level stations for the calculation of passage authorizations in the SorelMontreal sector of the navigational waterway, namely Sorel, Contrecoeur, Varennes, Montreal-Frontenac and Montreal-Jetty No. 1.
In light of the particular features of the navigational waterway in the portion between buoys M84 (downstream of the municipality of Verchères) and M11 (downstream of the Bellmouth curve), it was agreed to adjust upward the available water column by 10 cm in this portion.
The minimum water column in this portion of the navigational waterway as per the Contrecur hydrographic station, obtained after adjustment, will be used for the calculation of under-keel clearance.

properties.title: NW-C-1838-24 · Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance
properties.rawText:
Canadian Coast Guard Marine Communications and Traffic Services have been using all Canadian Hydrographic Service water-level stations for the calculation of passage authorizations in the SorelMontreal sector of the navigational waterway, namely Sorel, Contrecoeur, Varennes, Montreal-Frontenac and Montreal-Jetty No. 1.
In light of the particular features of the navigational waterway in the portion between buoys M84 (downstream of the municipality of Verchères) and M157 (opposite to the Port of Montreal, section 109) as well as the No. 1 Anchorage Pointe-aux-Tremble, it was agreed to adjust upward the available water column by 10 cm in this portion.
The minimum water column in this portion of the navigational waterway as per the Varennes hydrographic station, obtained after adjustment, will be used for the calculation of under-keel clearance.
Monthly Notice to Mariners Eastern Edition 08/22 refers.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 8 at 5:53PM AST until November 8 at 8:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Naguabo...

* WHEN...Until 800 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable. Expect
many areas of slow moving or standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 552 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area.
- At 550 PM AST, emergency management reported that road PR-31 km
8.0 remains closed due flooding waters.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flash Flood Warning issued November 8 at 1:23PM CST until November 8 at 8:00PM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX

FFWEWX

The National Weather Service in Austin/San Antonio has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Western Bandera County in south central Texas...
Edwards County in south central Texas...
Northwestern Kerr County in south central Texas...
Northern Kinney County in south central Texas...
Real County in south central Texas...
Northern Uvalde County in south central Texas...
Northeastern Val Verde County in south central Texas...

* Until 800 PM CST Sunday.

* At 123 PM CST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
along highways where low water crossings exist.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Medina, Rocksprings, Leakey, Loma Alta, Vanderpool, Camp Wood,
Vance, Barksdale, Montell, Tuff, Reagan Wells, Rio Frio, Garner
State Park, Carta Valley, Lost Maples State Natural Area, Concan,
Kerr Wildlife Management Area, Utopia, Devil's Sinkhole State
Natural Area and Kickapoo Cavern State Park.

At 1:21 PM, Edwards County Emergency Management reported several low
water crossings near Barksdale were flooded, some of which were
impassable.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

to rise in Action Stage. The river is forecast to climb into Minor
flood stage into early next week amd continue a steady rise in Minor
Flood stage through next week.

forecast.

pool enclosures and patios in the Stone Island area.

through flooded areas.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Verde River between Fort McDowell and the
Salt River is occurring. Recreation on or near the Verde River will
be unsafe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 726 AM MST, A streamflow gauge on the Verde River near the
Salt River confluence measured a flow exceeding 1800 cfs.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Fort McDowell and any recreational areas along the Verde River
downstream towards the confluence with the Salt River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring. It is important to know where you are relative
to streams, rivers, or creeks. Campers and hikers should avoid
streams or creeks.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam releases continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Salt River below Granite Reef Dam is
occurring. Flooding of low water crossings across the Salt River
upstream of Tempe Town Lake, including McKellips Road, is
occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 712 AM MST, dam operators reported around 1400 cfs was being
released from Granite Reef Dam. Additionally, a streamflow gauge
downstream of Granite Reef Dam measured a flow around 2000 cfs.
Flooding due to a dam floodgate release will continue.
- Flooding is occurring along the Salt River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Salt River between Granite Reef Dam and Tempe Town Lake.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

to streams, rivers, or creeks. Campers and hikers should avoid
streams or creeks.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 8 at 7:12AM MST until November 9 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam releases continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. Low-water crossings are
inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 709 AM MST, upstream floodgate release from Tempe Town Lake
and continued releases from Granite Reef Dam farther upstream has
lead to flooding in the warned area. A US Army Corps of Engineers
streamflow gauge on the Gila River showed the flow near Old US 80
was around 1000 cfs. Another automated gauge reported that the
current pool elevation of Painted Rock Lake was around 571 feet.
- Flooding is occurring along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Goodyear, Painted Rock Dam, Liberty, Phoenix International
Raceway and Arlington.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 8 at 8:51AM EST by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Peace River At Arcadia at SR 70 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Peace River at Arcadia at SR 70.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 15.5 feet, 25 homes at River Acres are impacted.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 15.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Sunday was 16.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 11.1 feet Friday
morning.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.3
feet on 08/19/1939.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 900 PM EST.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flash Flood Warning issued November 8 at 5:13PM CST until November 8 at 8:00PM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX

At 513 PM CST, emergency management reported flooding across the
warned area with several roads flooded, including around US highway
377, from Erwin Draw. Areas near Kickapoo Cavern State Park and
Devils River Natural Area - Del Norte from Dolan Creek have flooding
as well. Between 2 and 5 inches of rain have fallen over the past 24
to 36 hours. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in
the warned area.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Recent rains producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, along
highways where low water crossings exist.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rocksprings, Loma Alta, Carta Valley, Vinegarone, Kickapoo Cavern
State Park, Devils River State Nat Area Del Norte, Devil's Sinkhole
State Natural Area, Devils River State Nat Area Big Satan, Devils
Shores and Pafford Crossing.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

Marine Weather Statement issued November 8 at 6:30PM AST by NWS San Juan PR

The areas affected include...
Anegada Passage east of Virgin Gorda and Saint Croix south to 17N...
Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including the
coastal waters of Saint Croix...

* At 630 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. These strong
thunderstorms were located over the offshore Caribbean waters,
about 5 nm SE of St. Croix, moving northeast at 10 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Anegada Passage east of Virgin Gorda and
Saint Croix south to 17N and Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from
10 NM to 17N, including the coastal waters of Saint Croix.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.

Freezing rain is expected over portions of the Trans-Labrador Highway.

Locations: Kenamu River to Red Bay (inland and over higher terrain).

Time span: tonight.

Remarks: Precipitation is expected to fall as rain in coastal areas, while colder temperatures inland and over higher elevations will support a period of freezing rain. Over parts of the Eagle River region, the freezing rain may be preceded by a period of ice pellets.

Freezing rain could persist for several hours in some locations, resulting in ice accretion and slippery surfaces. Consider adjusting travel plans to avoid the most adverse conditions.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are expected.

Strong southeasterly winds.

When: Overnight tonight into Monday afternoon.

Where: Haida Gwaii and North Vancouver Island.

A low pressure system is tracking towards the BC coast and strong southeasterly winds 90 gusting to 110 km/h will develop ahead of the system by early Monday morning. These winds will continue into Monday afternoon before weakening. 

Another low pressure is following on its heels and the winds will once again likely  reach warning criteria before morning on Tuesday and maybe extended to other regions.

Local utility outages are possible.

Secure loose objects. Stay away from fallen power lines.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Extended periods of blizzard conditions with poor visibility in blowing snow are expected.

Where: Dempster Highway, near the Richardson Mountains.

When: Now through Tuesday morning.

Remarks: Strong easterly winds have materialized near the Richardson mountains today. Winds will likely remain strong through tonight, ease somewhat on Monday morning then further increase again Monday afternoon.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 8 at 7:49PM AST until November 8 at 10:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Naguabo...

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Low-water crossings are inundated
with water and may not be passable. Expect many areas of slow
moving or standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 746 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area.
- At 745 PM AST, emergency management reported that road PR-31
remains closed due flood waters due to inundation along Rio
Blanco.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.rawText:
Maximum wind gusts: southeasterly 100 km/h in the Wreckhouse area.

Time span: ending this evening.

High-sided vehicles will be pushed around by the wind. Disruptions to services and travel are possible.

Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.rawText:
Gale Warning issued November 8 at 10:14PM EST until November 9 at 4:00AM EST by NWS Detroit/Pontiac MI

* WHAT...Expect sustained winds up to 30 knots from the
northwest with gusts up to 35 knots. The largest significant
waves will be 11 feet with a potential maximum wave height of
16 feet.

* WHERE...Lake Huron from 5NM east of Mackinac Bridge to Presque
Isle Lt beyond 5 NM off shore and Lake Huron from Presque Isle
Light to Sturgeon Point MI beyond 5NM off shore.

* WHEN...The maximum winds are expected around 11 PM EST Sunday
with the largest waves expected around 2 AM EST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous waves which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.

Flood Warning issued November 8 at 8:11PM CST until November 11 at 1:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Oso Creek Near Corpus Christi affecting Nueces County.

For the Oso Creek...including Corpus Christi...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Oso Creek near Corpus Christi.

* WHEN...From Monday morning to Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding occurs from the
headwaters near Violet Road, or FM 24, to Oso Bay. Secondary roads
and low bridges near the creek are also flooded.

At 25.0 feet, Major flooding reaches the approaches to the Farm to
Market 763 bridge. Numerous outbuildings and barns are surrounded,
and flow approaches apartment buildings below Farm to Market 763.
Kings Crossing Golf Course is at least 1/2 flooded. Water is within 3
feet of some homes. Water flows across Oso Parkway Road at 2 low
areas in the extreme south portion of the Lakes Subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM CST Sunday the stage was 11.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to climb above flood stage
Monday morning to a crest near 23 feet late Monday night. It will
then fall below flood stage late Tuesday night.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flash Flood Warning issued November 8 at 7:46PM CST until November 9 at 12:00AM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX

FFWEWX

The National Weather Service in Austin/San Antonio has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Edwards County in south central Texas...
Northwestern Kinney County in south central Texas...
Northeastern Val Verde County in south central Texas...

* Until midnight CST.

* At 746 PM CST, emergency management and TxDot reports flooding
across the warned area with several roads flooded and closed,
including near US highway 377, SH 55 and CR 450. A water rescue was
reported this evening in the Newby Hills subdivision along CR 450.
Areas near Kickapoo Cavern State Park and Devils River Natural Area
- Del Norte have flooding as well. Between 2 and 5 inches of rain
have fallen over the past 24 to 36 hours. Additional rainfall
amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned area.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rocksprings, Loma Alta, Carta Valley, Vinegarone, Kickapoo Cavern
State Park, Devils River State Nat Area Del Norte, Devil's Sinkhole
State Natural Area, Devils River State Nat Area Big Satan, Devils
Shores and Pafford Crossing.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

river may rise slightly early this week and remain in Major flood
stage through at least Friday.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Sunday the stage was 16.97 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Sunday was 16.97 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 17.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
What:
Moderate to strong gusty winds.

When:
Now till early Monday morning.

Where:
- McGregor
- B.C. South Peace River

Additional information:
An incoming cold front will bring a strong push of southwesterly winds, with gusts potentially reaching 80 km/h starting this afternoon. These gusty winds are expected to ease overnight.

Local utility outages are possible. 
Secure loose objects.
High-sided vehicles will be pushed around by the wind.
Parks and forests will likely sustain some damage.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 8 at 11:42PM MST until November 9 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam releases continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. Low-water crossings may be
inundated with water and not passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1128 PM MST, upstream floodgate release from Tempe Town Lake
has lead to flooding in the warned area. A US Army Corps of
Engineers streamflow gauge on the Gila River showed the flow near
Old US 80 was around 700 cfs. Another automated gauge reported
that the current pool elevation of Painted Rock Lake was around
572 feet.
- Flooding is occurring along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Painted Rock Dam, Liberty, and Arlington.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are expected.

Strong southeasterly winds 90 km/h gusting to 110.

When: Now through this afternoon. Overnight tonight through Tuesday.

Where: Haida Gwaii and North Vancouver Island.

Additional information:
A series of strong storms will bring periods of strong southeast winds in the next couple of days.

The first system is tracking towards the BC coast and strong southeasterly winds 90 gusting to 110 km/h will develop ahead of it early this morning. These winds will ease this afternoon. 

Another low pressure system is following on its heels, and the winds will once again reach warning criteria overnight. Winds will ease somewhat Tuesday morning but yet another storm will bring strong southeasterly winds by Tuesday afternoon.

Local utility outages are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects. Stay away from fallen power lines.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

THE FOLLOWING OPS ARE NOT AUTH WI THIS TFR: FLT TRAINING, PRACTICE INSTRUMENT APCH, AEROBATIC FLT, GLIDER OPS, PARACHUTE OPS, ULTRALIGHT, HANG GLIDING, BALLOON OPS, AGRICULTURE/CROP DUSTING, ANIMAL POPULATION CTL FLT OPS, BANNER TOWING OPS, SIGHTSEEING OPS, MAINTENANCE TEST FLIGHTS, MODEL ACFT OPS, MODEL ROCKETRY, UNMANNED ACFT SYSTEMS (UAS), AND UTILITY AND PIPELINE SURVEY OPS.

Flood Warning issued November 9 at 5:02PM CST until November 11 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX

...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Texas...

Llano River at Llano affecting Llano County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Llano River at Llano.

* WHEN...From this evening to Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding makes secondary
roads and low bridges in the flood plain dangerous to motorists
including the low water crossing of Ranch Road 3404/Slab Road near
Kingsland. Equipment should be moved from low docks and boat ties
loosened downstream in Kingsland.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:00 PM CST Monday the stage was 4.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this evening to a crest of 13.2 feet tomorrow morning. It will
then fall below flood stage tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.6
feet on 06/01/2016.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 515 AM CST.

in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,

properties.title: Yellow advisory · fog advisory
properties.rawText:
Dense fog continues.

Fog is expected to persist until late Tuesday morning.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NTstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NTStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: Ft. Simpson Region including Jean Marie River

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are expected.

Strong southeasterly winds 90 km/h gusting to 110.

When: Overnight tonight through Tuesday.

Where: Haida Gwaii and North Vancouver Island.

Additional information:
A series of strong storms will bring periods of strong southeast winds in the next couple of days.

Winds are currently easing this evening from the last system. 

Another low pressure system is following on its heels, and the winds will once again reach warning criteria overnight. Winds will ease somewhat Tuesday morning but yet another storm will bring strong southeasterly winds by Tuesday afternoon.

Local utility outages are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects. Stay away from fallen power lines.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · winter storm warning
properties.rawText:
Hazardous winter conditions are expected due to:
- Snow
- Blowing snow

Where: Haines Road, south of Bear Camp.

When: Ongoing through to midnight.

Remarks: A winter storm will bring snow to the Haines Road today. Gusty winds will likely accompany the snow, particularly tonight with blowing snow possibly reducing visibilities.

Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: Haines Road - Haines Junction to Pleasant Camp

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Extended periods of blizzard conditions with poor visibility in blowing snow are expected.

Where: Dempster Highway, near the Richardson Mountains.

When: Now through Tuesday morning.

Remarks: Moderate easterly winds near the Richardson mountains will strengthen to 70 gusting to 100 km/h this evening. The strong winds will persist through Tuesday morning.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

properties.title: Orange warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Very heavy rain is expected.

Where: West and central Vancouver Island.

When: Tuesday morning through overnight Wednesday.

What: 150 to 200 mm of rain, possibly exceeding 250 mm locally.

Remarks: A very robust frontal system is set to make landfall on Vancouver Island very early Tuesday morning. Rain, heavy at times, will persist until Wednesday morning. Even though the heaviest rain eases by Wednesday morning, moderate precipitation is expected to continue until Thursday morning.

Localized flooding is likely. Some roads may become impassable. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Stay away from rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: West Vancouver Island; Inland Vancouver Island

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 10 at 6:35AM CST until November 11 at 5:00AM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX

...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Texas...

Devils River At Pafford Crossing nr Comstock affecting Val Verde
County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Devils River at Pafford Crossing nr Comstock.

* WHEN...Until late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, (1.8 meters), Moderate lowland flooding over
1/4 mile wide covers the right bank to the canyon walls. The
turbulent flow can wash motorists, campers, and equipment
downstream from Pafford Crossing to Amistad Reservoir. Livestock
are cut off and potentially drowned below Juno to Amistad
Reservoir.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:15 AM CST Tuesday the stage was 7.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:15 AM CST Tuesday was 7.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this afternoon and continue falling to 3.3 feet Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.2
feet on 10/19/2018.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 645 PM CST.

late this morning. It will then fall below flood stage late this
afternoon.

feet on 06/01/2016.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

after 7 AM PST today.

47 knots has significantly increased, but the specific timing
and/or location is still uncertain. It is intended to provide
additional lead time for mariners who may wish to consider
altering their plans.

Gale Warning issued November 10 at 1:20AM PST until November 11 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR

* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, Rough bar conditions
expected with seas 11 to 16 ft at 13 seconds and south winds 20
to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt. For the Gale Warning, seas 12
to 16 ft at 14 seconds and south winds 30 to 35 kt with gusts up
to 40 kt expected.

* WHERE...In the Main Channel of the Columbia River Bar.

* WHEN...Small Craft Advisory, until 10 AM PST this morning.
Gale Warning, from 10 AM this morning to 4 PM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

A Gale Warning means winds of 34 to 47 knots are imminent or
occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

out 10 NM and Waters from Cape Foulweather to Florence OR from

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or cause
damage to vessels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Isolated gale force wind gusts expected

imminent or occurring. Recreational boaters should remain in
port, or take shelter until waves subside.  Commercial vessels
should prepare for rough seas and consider remaining in port or
taking shelter in port until hazardous seas subside.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Strong winds are expected.

Where: East Vancouver Island - Nanoose Bay to Campbell River, Sunshine Coast - Saltery Bay to Powell River.

When: Late this afternoon until early Wednesday morning.

What: Southeast winds 70 gusting to 90 km/h.

Remarks: A very robust frontal system makes landfall over the South Coast very early this morning. Strong southeasterly winds will develop through the day and will peak at 70 km/h gusting to 90 by late this afternoon. These strong winds will persist through the night before easing early Wednesday morning.

Local utility outages are possible. Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects. Be prepared to adapt your driving for changing conditions.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are expected.

Strong southeasterly winds 90 km/h gusting to 110.

When: This afternoon until late this evening.

Where: Haida Gwaii and North Vancouver Island.

Additional information:
Another frontal system will approach the coast today and the winds will once again reach warning criteria this afternoon. The winds will ease overnight tonight as the system departs.

Local utility outages are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects. Stay away from fallen power lines.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is expected.

Where: Whistler and Pemberton.

When: This morning until Thursday morning.

What: 50 to 100 mm of rain.

Remarks: A very robust frontal system makes landfall on the South Coast very early this morning. Light rain increases to moderate to heavy rain this afternoon and persists overnight. There may be a slight easing of rainfall rates during the day on Wednesday before intensifying once again late in the afternoon.

Total rainfall accumulations are expected to reach 50 to 100 mm during this multiday event in the vicinity of Whistler with lesser, but still significant amounts for Pemberton. This region will remain closely monitored throughout the event.

Rain will ease Thursday morning.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning

Where: Metro Vancouver - North Shore including West Vancouver and North Vancouver.

When: This morning until late Wednesday night.

Remarks: A very robust frontal system makes landfall on the South Coast very early this morning. Rainfall rates will intensity this afternoon and overnight, reaching up to 5 to 10 mm/h for several hours. The heavy rain is expected to ease slightly during the day on Wednesday before increasing once again late in the day. Heavy rainfall will end late Wednesday night.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

When: Tuesday morning to Wednesday night

What: 50 to 100 mm of rain.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is expected.

What: Rainfall approaching or exceeding 100 mm

Where: Areas in the vicinity of Quatsino, Port Alice and Woss.

When: Showers beginning this morning and developing into heavy rain this afternoon and persisting until Wednesday morning. 

Remarks: An approaching frontal system later today will bring up to 100 mm of rainfall to the western sections of the region by Wednesday morning. After a series of storms that have impacted the region, the ground is saturated which increases the likelihood of impacts.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Parks and forests will likely sustain some damage. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Extended periods of blizzard conditions with poor visibility in blowing snow are expected.

Where: Dempster Highway, near the Richardson Mountains.

When: This morning.

Remarks: Easterly winds of 80 km/h gusting to 110 continue early this morning but will ease below thresholds by mid morning.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

properties.title: Orange warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Very heavy rain is expected.

Where: Howe Sound, and Sea to Sky Highway - Squamish to Whistler.

When: This morning to Thursday morning.

What: 120 to 160 mm, possibly more.

Remarks: A very robust frontal system makes landfall over the South Coast very early this morning. Rainfall rates will intensify this afternoon and persist overnight, reaching to up 5 to 10 mm/h or more for several hours. There may be a slight easing of rainfall rates during the day on Wednesday before intensifying once again late in the afternoon.

Total rainfall accumulations are expected to reach 120 to 160 mm during this multiday event. Howe Sound and the Sea to Sky Highway regions will remain closely monitored as there is the potential for higher total rainfall accumulations.

Localized flooding is likely. Some roads may become impassable. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Stay away from rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 10 at 1:15PM CST until November 11 at 5:20PM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Llano River at Llano affecting Llano County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Llano River at Llano.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding makes secondary
roads and low bridges in the flood plain dangerous to motorists
including the low water crossing of Ranch Road 3404/Slab Road near
Kingsland. Equipment should be moved from low docks and boat ties
loosened downstream in Kingsland.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:00 PM CST Tuesday the stage was 14.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:00 PM CST Tuesday was 14.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tonight and continue falling to 3.8 feet early Sunday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.6
feet on 06/01/2016.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 115 AM CST.

to streams, rivers, or creeks. Campers and hikers should avoid
streams or creeks.

properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 10 at 9:29AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream has resulted in river
levels just below Moderate flood stage. River levels are expected to
remain steady near Moderate Flood stage through this week and into
the weekend as a large volume of water works north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Tuesday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise slightly to 3 feet late
this week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
What: Strong and damaging southeasterly winds are expected.

When: Overnight into Wednesday afternoon.

Where: Highway 97 - Clinton to 100 Mile House via Begbie Summit, 100 Mile, Cariboo.

Additional Information:
Another strong and slow moving frontal system will lie across central B.C. tonight through Wednesday. Southeasterly wind will increase to 30 km/h gusting to 50 near noon, then strengthen further Wednesday morning with gusts to 70 km/h. Winds will continue to increase to 50 km/h gusting up to 90 through Wednesday afternoon before easing Wednesday evening.

Local utility outages are possible. High-sided vehicles will be pushed around by the wind.

Secure loose objects. Stay away from fallen power lines. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services, and utilities.

Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions with poor visibility in blowing snow are expected to persist until Wednesday morning.

Strong east winds gusting up to 70 km/h will bring poor visibility in blowing snow today and tonight.

Winds will weaken slightly before morning, bringing some improvement to visibility, but blowing snow is possible until mid day on Wednesday.

Travel will likely be hazardous.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NTstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NTStorm.

When: Overnight into Wednesday afternoon.

Where: Chilcotin - South of Highway 20 including Tatlayoko Lake, Big Creek and Dog Creek. 

Additional Information:
Another strong and slow moving frontal system will lie across central B.C. tonight through Wednesday. Winds will continue to increase to 60 km/h gusting to 100 or more through Wednesday afternoon before easing Wednesday evening.

Utility outages are likely. Driving conditions will likely be very difficult. There is a risk of injury due to flying or falling debris.

Secure loose objects. Stay away from fallen power lines. Prepare for some disruptions to transportation, services, and utilities.

Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

Where: Stuart-Nechako, and Prince George region.

properties.title: Hazardous Seas Warning
properties.rawText:
Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 10 at 1:50PM PST until November 11 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR

* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and steep
swell dominated seas 10 to 14 ft at 14 seconds. South winds
increase late tonight, 25 to 35 kt. Gale force gusts to 40 kt
are possible at times tonight through Wednesday with seas
becoming very steep and increasing to 14 to 16 ft at 14
seconds.

* WHERE...All areas.

* WHEN...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, until 4 PM PST
Wednesday. For the Small Craft Advisory, from 4 PM Wednesday to
10 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds and/or very steep and hazardous seas
could capsize or damage vessels. Bar crossings will become
especially treacherous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong front will bring gales and the
potential for storm force wind gusts Thursday night into Friday
followed by a very large westerly ocean swell Friday night into
Saturday. Very steep, hazardous waves could reach 25 to 30 feet
or higher. Please stay tuned for updates on this high impact
weather pattern.

* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks

Recreational boaters should remain in port. Commercial vessels
should prepare for very steep seas and consider remaining in port
until conditions improve.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Strong gusty winds tonight.

Where: Near Haro Strait.

What: Southeasterly winds gusting to 90 km/h.

Additional information:
Strong southeasterly winds gusting to 90 km/h will develop early this evening near Haro Strait as a robust frontal system approaches the South Coast. The winds will ease overnight.

Local utility outages are possible. Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are expected.

Strong southeasterly winds 90 km/h gusting to 110.

When: Now until tonight.

Where: Haida Gwaii and North Vancouver Island.

Additional information:
Another frontal system will approach the coast and the winds will once again reach warning criteria this evening. The winds will ease overnight tonight as the system departs.

Local utility outages are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects. Stay away from fallen power lines.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

Damaging winds are expected.

What: Strong and damaging gusty southerly winds.

Where: 
South Thompson – Western sections from Spences Bridge to Cache Creek, including Ashcroft, and the Thompson Highlands including Logan Lake, Fraser Canyon - south including Lytton

When: Wednesday.

A strong and slow moving Pacific frontal system will lie across central B.C. tonight through Wednesday. Southerly winds of 50 km/h gusting up to 80 to 90 will develop Wednesday morning and last into afternoon.

Wind will ease to light through Wednesday evening.

Local utility outages are possible.

Secure loose objects. Stay away from fallen power lines.

What: Rainfall approaching or exceeding 100 mm

Where: Areas in the vicinity of Quatsino, Port Alice and Woss.

When: Now until Wednesday morning. 

Remarks: An approaching frontal system will bring 100 to 120 mm of rainfall to the western sections of the region by Wednesday morning. After a series of storms that have impacted the region, the ground is saturated which increases the likelihood of impacts.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Parks and forests will likely sustain some damage. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions with poor visibility in snow and blowing snow will develop Wednesday morning and persist until Thursday morning.

Snowfall will begin overnight tonight, and continue through Friday. Upwards of 20 to 30 cm of new snow is expected. 

Moderate southeast winds will strengthen Wednesday morning, gusting up to 70 km/h and causing reduced visibility in blowing snow.

Winds are expected to weaken Thursday morning, although there will be some reduced visibility in snow and blowing snow until Friday afternoon.

Travel will likely be hazardous.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

Blizzard warnings are issued when widespread poor visibility in blowing snow is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 11 at 12:54AM CST until November 11 at 1:30AM CST by NWS Houston/Galveston TX

SMWHGX

The National Weather Service in League City has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Freeport to Matagorda Ship Channel TX from 20 to 60
NM...

* Until 130 AM CST.

* At 1254 AM CST, a strong thunderstorm was located 7 nm northeast of
Buoy 42019, moving east at around 25 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Galveston A171.

Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.
Wind gusts 34 knots or greater, small hail, high waves, dangerous
lightning, and heavy rain are possible with this storm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 10 at 10:02PM PST until November 11 at 4:01PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rainfall over the Olympics earlier today has mostly ended, but
flooding on the Skokomish River will continue into Wednesday the the
flood crest moves downstream.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM PST Tuesday the stage was 17.4 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 PM PST Tuesday was 17.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river will crest around 17.5 feet later tonight.
It will then fall below flood stage around midday Wednesday.
Another return to flood stage is possible late this week.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 715 AM PST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 10 at 7:47PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream has resulted in river
levels just below Moderate flood stage. River levels are expected to
remain steady near Moderate Flood stage through this week and into
the weekend as a large volume of water works north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Tuesday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise slightly to 3 feet late
this week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Accumulating snowfall is expected inland and over higher terrain.

Locations: Gros Morne to Hawkes Bay. 

Potential snowfall: 20 to 30 cm, highest over elevated terrain. 

Time span: Wednesday morning until Thursday evening. 

Remarks: Snow will accumulate steadily inland and over higher terrain while rain, or rain mixed with snow, is expected near the coast.

Snow may lead to adverse travel conditions, with slippery conditions in some locations, particularly over higher elevations.

Be prepared for winter driving conditions, keep a snow brush handy, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.
properties.stationOrArea: Gros Morne; Parson's Pond - Hawke's Bay

properties.title: Yellow advisory · fog advisory
properties.rawText:
Dense fog has reduced visibility to near zero over parts of southern Saskatchewan.

The fog is expected to lift later in the morning or near noon.

Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Be prepared for areas of near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach your destination. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Fog advisories are issued when widespread poor visibility in fog is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #SKStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: City of Regina; R.M. of Maple Bush including Riverhurst and Douglas Prov. Park; R.M. of Huron including Tugaske and 96 more areas

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions with poor visibility in blowing snow will continue until Wednesday morning, with strong east winds gusting up to 70 km/h.

Winds will weaken slightly before morning, bringing some improvement to visibility, but blowing snow is possible until mid day on Wednesday.

Travel will likely be hazardous.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NTstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NTStorm.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
sturdy building.
