properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 11 at 3:39AM PST until November 11 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...Observed flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rainfall over the Olympics has ended, but flooding on the
Skokomish River will continue into late this morning as the flood
crest moves downstream.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and minor flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 17.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 AM PST Wednesday was 17.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage midday
and continue falling to near 15.0 feet late tonight.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.6
feet on 10/20/2003.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at noon PST.

properties.rawText:
Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 11 at 1:50AM PST until November 11 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR

* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 kt with very steep and hazardous
seas 14 to 16 ft at 14 seconds. Gale force gusts to 40 kt are
possible at times through this morning. South winds ease to 15
to 25 kt this afternoon and swell dominated seas remain steep 12
to 15 ft. Conditions rapidly worsen late Thursday as south winds
and seas quickly increase. Gales of 30 to 40 kt with gusts to 50
kt possible. Seas increase due to increasing wind waves and an
incoming heavy long period swell, possibly reaching 20 to 25 ft
at 15 seconds Friday.

* WHERE...All areas.

* WHEN...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the Small Craft Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 10 PM PST Thursday. For the Gale Watch, from
Thursday evening through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds and very steep seas could capsize or
damage vessels. Low visibility conditions are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Very steep, hazardous seas could reach 25
to 30 feet or higher late Friday into Saturday as a heavy long
period swell continues to build in. Please stay tuned for
updates on this high impact weather pattern.

* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks

very steep seas. Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course,
and/or secure the vessel for severe conditions.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Accumulating snowfall is expected.

Locations: Upper Lake Melville.

Potential snowfall: 10 to 15 cm or more (mainly over higher terrain).

Time span: late this afternoon until Thursday morning. 

Remarks:  Snow may mix with, or change to, rain at times over the lower elevations of the Upper Lake Melville area. The greatest snowfall amounts are expected over higher terrain. 

Motorists planning travel along the Trans-Labrador Highway are advised that a snowfall warning is in effect, with higher amounts expected between Cache River and Crooks Lake.

Snow accumulation may make travel slow or hazardous. Roads and walkways could become slippery and difficult to navigate.

Be prepared for winter driving conditions, keep a snow brush handy, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.title: Yellow watch · winter storm watch
properties.rawText:
A hazardous winter storm is expected to begin Wednesday night, bringing damaging winds and poor visibility in blowing snow.

Strong, persistent south winds will develop this morning and intensify tonight into Thursday. Gusts between 80 to 90 km/h are expected beginning early Thursday morning.

These strong winds combined with falling snow are expected to cause poor visibility in blowing snow through the day on Thursday.

Visibility may be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times. Local utility outages are possible.

Consider rescheduling travel and outdoor activities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning

Snow will begin this morning and continue through Friday before tapering off Friday evening.

Additionally, easterly winds gusting up to 50 km/h are expected to develop late this afternoon and continue into tonight, which may result in blowing snow at times.

Travel will likely be challenging. Visibility will likely be reduced at times.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 11 at 11:30AM PST until November 11 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until this evening.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:30 AM PST Wednesday was 17.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall below flood stage late this
afternoon to 14.3 feet late tonight. It will then rise to 14.4
feet late tomorrow morning. It will fall to 14.1 feet late
tomorrow evening. It will then rise above flood stage Friday
afternoon to 17.4 feet late Saturday morning. It will fall again
but remain above flood stage.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.3
feet on 03/06/2014.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1000 PM PST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 11 at 11:41AM MST until November 17 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1138 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue.
The amount of water released will increase during the next couple
of days, peaking at 3000 cfs.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Accumulating snowfall is expected inland and over higher terrain.

Locations: Gros Morne to Hawkes Bay. 

Potential snowfall: 20 to 30 cm, highest over elevated terrain. 

Time span: continuing until Thursday evening. 

Remarks: Snow will accumulate steadily inland and over higher terrain while rain, or rain mixed with snow, is expected near the coast.

Snow may lead to adverse travel conditions, with slippery conditions in some locations, particularly over higher elevations.

Be prepared for winter driving conditions, keep a snow brush handy, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.
properties.stationOrArea: Gros Morne; Parson's Pond - Hawke's Bay

Potential snowfall: 10 to 15 cm or more (mainly over higher terrain).

Time span: continuing until Thursday morning. 

Remarks:  Snow may mix with, or change to, rain at times over the lower elevations of the Upper Lake Melville area. The greatest snowfall amounts are expected over higher terrain. 

Motorists planning travel along the Trans-Labrador Highway are advised that a snowfall warning is in effect, with higher amounts expected between Cache River and Crooks Lake.

Snow accumulation may make travel slow or hazardous. Roads and walkways could become slippery and difficult to navigate.

Be prepared for winter driving conditions, keep a snow brush handy, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Winter weather travel statement in effect.

What:
Local snowfall amounts of 5 to 10 cm possible along with hazardous travel conditions.

Where:
Along the Highway 17 corridor from Dubreuiville Corners to White River and along the Highway 519 corridor to the town of Dubreuiville.

When:
Snow is expected to end later this afternoon or early this evening.

Motorists should expect hazardous winter driving conditions and adjust travel plans accordingly. Travel may be hazardous due to sudden changes in the weather.

Slow down driving in slippery conditions. Watch for taillights ahead and maintain a safe following distance.

For road conditions and other traveller information from the Ministry of Transportation, visit https://www.ontario.ca/511, https://x.com/511Ontario, or call 5-1-1.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: Yellow advisory · fog advisory
properties.rawText:
Dense fog has reduced visibility to near-zero over parts of southeast Saskatchewan.

The fog is expected to lift late in the afternoon.

Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Be prepared for areas of near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach your destination. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Fog advisories are issued when widespread poor visibility in fog is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #SKStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: R.M. of Maple Bush including Riverhurst and Douglas Prov. Park; R.M. of Huron including Tugaske; R.M. of Eyebrow including Eyebrow and Brownlee and 23 more areas

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
Significant snowfall is expected over some areas. 

Locations: Eagle River- west of Crooks Lake, and Churchill Valley - east of Cache River. 

Total snowfall: 15 to 20 cm. 

Time span: continuing until Thursday morning. 

Remarks: The heaviest snowfall is expected to occur tonight. Precipitation will transition to rain over Eagle River - west of Crooks Lake by early Thursday morning and for Churchill Valley by noon on Thursday.

Travel will likely be challenging.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions.

Snowfall warnings are issued when significant impacts are expected due to snowfall accumulations.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
A prolonged period of snow, with total accumulations of 15 to 25 cm by Friday evening is expected.

Snow will continue through Friday before tapering off in the evening.

Additionally, easterly winds gusting up to 50 km/h are expected to develop which may result in blowing snow at times.

Travel will likely be challenging. Visibility will likely be reduced at times.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Wind gusts to 90 km/h are expected.

Winds will strengthen overnight, continue through Thursday, and be accompanied by reduced visibility in widespread blowing snow. 

These winds will diminish on Thursday evening, although they will continue to be gusty into Friday.

Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are occurring.

Where: East Vancouver Island - Nanoose Bay to Campbell River, Sunshine Coast - Saltery Bay to Powell River.

When: Now until later afternoon.

What: Southeast winds 70 gusting to 90 km/h.

Remarks: A very robust frontal system is bringing strong winds to the South Coast. Strong southeasterly winds will persist early this afternoon before easing below warning criteria later this afternoon

Local utility outages are possible. Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects. Be prepared to adapt your driving for changing conditions.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: East Vancouver Island - Nanoose Bay to Fanny Bay; East Vancouver Island - Courtenay to Campbell River; Sunshine Coast - Saltery Bay to Powell River

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is occurring.

Where: Metro Vancouver - North Shore including West Vancouver and North Vancouver.

When: Now until tonight.

What: 60 to 100 mm of rain, possibly near 120 mm in the mountains.

Remarks: A very robust frontal system is bringing rain to the South Coast. Rain, heavy at times, will return this afternoon and  continue through this evening before tapering off tonight.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: Metro Vancouver - North Shore including West Vancouver and North Vancouver

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions with poor visibility in snow and blowing snow will develop this evening and persist until Thursday afternoon.

Snow will continue through Friday with 20 to 30 cm of new snow expected.

Southeast winds will gust up to 70 km/h, causing reduced visibility in blowing snow. Winds will begin to weaken Thursday afternoon.

Travel will likely be hazardous.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

Blizzard warnings are issued when widespread poor visibility in blowing snow is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Orange warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are expected.

When: Now until early this evening.

Where: Prince George region.

Additional Information:
Another strong and slow moving frontal system will lie across central B.C. today. South 60 km/h gusting to 90 will continue this afternoon will ease early this evening.

Utility outages are likely. High-sided vehicles could be overturned by the wind.

Secure loose objects. If outside, protect yourself from flying or falling debris. Stay away from fallen power lines. Prepare for some disruptions to transportation, services, and utilities.

Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 11 at 8:59PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

The areas affected include...
Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 20-60 nm...

* At 859 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. This strong
thunderstorm was located 53 NM east of Port Canaveral, moving east
at 10 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian
Inlet 20-60 nm.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 11 at 8:46PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to remain just below Minor flood stage. The river is forecast to
slowly climb into Minor flood stage later this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Water surrounds homes and covers some
driveways in the Stone Island area near Enterprise in Volusia
County. Water enters yards and floods docks in the River Oaks
Estates subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 5.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to Minor Flood Stage
early Friday morning, where it will linger near 5.5 feet into
early next week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 1215 PM EST.

properties.rawText:
Gale Warning issued November 11 at 3:43PM HST until November 12 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI

* WHAT...Northeast winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 45 kt and
seas up to 14 feet.

* WHERE...Maalaea Bay, Pailolo Channel, Alenuihaha Channel, Big
Island Leeward Waters and Big Island Southeast Waters.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels.

occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Winter weather travel statement in effect.

What:
Local snowfall amounts near 5 cm along with hazardous travel conditions.

Where:
Along the Highway 101 and Highway 651 corridors to the west of Chapleau and east of Wawa.
Areas south of  and including Chapleau along and west of the Highway 129 corridor.

When:
Snow is expected to end later this evening.

Motorists should expect hazardous winter driving conditions and adjust travel plans accordingly. Travel may be hazardous due to sudden changes in the weather. Surfaces such as highways, roads, walkways and parking lots may become difficult to navigate due to accumulating snow.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions.

For road conditions and other traveller information from the Ministry of Transportation, visit https://www.ontario.ca/511, https://x.com/511Ontario, or call 5-1-1.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Accumulating snowfall is expected inland and over higher terrain.

Locations: Gros Morne to Hawkes Bay. 

Potential snowfall: 20 to 30 cm, highest over elevated terrain. 

Time span: continuing until Thursday evening. 

Remarks: Snow will accumulate steadily inland and over higher terrain while rain, or rain mixed with snow, is expected near the coast.

Snow may lead to adverse travel conditions, with slippery conditions in some locations, particularly over higher elevations.

Be prepared for winter driving conditions, keep a snow brush handy, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Accumulating snowfall is expected.

Locations: Upper Lake Melville.

Potential snowfall: 10 to 15 cm or more (mainly over higher terrain).

Time span: continuing until Thursday morning. 

Remarks:  Snow may mix with, or change to, rain at times over the lower elevations of the Upper Lake Melville area. The greatest snowfall amounts are expected over higher terrain. 

Motorists planning travel along the Trans-Labrador Highway are advised that a snowfall warning is in effect, with higher amounts expected between Cache River and Crooks Lake.

Snow accumulation may make travel slow or hazardous. Roads and walkways could become slippery and difficult to navigate.

Be prepared for winter driving conditions, keep a snow brush handy, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.title: Yellow advisory · fog advisory
properties.rawText:
Near-zero visibility in fog continues.

A narrow but dense band of fog has reduced visibility to near-zero over parts of southern Saskatchewan. Visibilities may fluctuate in any given location as the band expands or shifts location overnight.

The fog is expected to lift midday on Thursday.

Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Be prepared for areas of near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach your destination. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Fog advisories are issued when widespread poor visibility in fog is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #SKStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is occurring.

What: Storm total of 50 to 80 mm.

Where: Chilcotin near the Coastal Mountains.

When: Tonight.

Additional Information:
A strong and slow moving frontal system lies across Central B.C. tonight. It will bring a total of 50 to 80 mm of rainfall to the western sections of Chilcotin by Thursday morning.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Some property damage is possible.

Avoid low-lying areas. Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Rainfall warnings are issued when significant impacts are expected due to rainfall amounts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Localized flooding is likely. Some roads may become impassable. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Stay away from rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisories, north winds 15 to 25 kt
with gusts up to 30 kt and waves 5 to 9 ft. For the Gale
Warning, north winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and
waves 6 to 11 ft expected.

* WHERE...Nearshore Waters from North Point Lighthouse to
Winthrop Harbor IL.

* WHEN...For the first Small Craft Advisory, until 6 AM CST
early this morning. For the Gale Warning, until 5 PM CST this
afternoon. For the second Small Craft Advisory, from 5 PM this
afternoon to midnight CST Friday night.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous waves which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for severe conditions.

Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 12 at 12:21AM PST until November 12 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR

* WHAT...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, very steep and hazardous
seas around 13 ft at 14 seconds and south winds 10 to 15 kt. For
the Small Craft Advisory, seas 13 to 14 ft at 14 seconds and
south winds 20 to 30 kt with isolated gusts up to 35 kt
expected. For the Gale Warning, seas 17 to 22 ft at 18 seconds
and south winds 30 to 40 kt with gusts up to 45 kt expected.

* WHERE...Waters from Cape Falcon to Cape Foulweather OR from 10
to 60 NM.

* WHEN...Hazardous Seas Warning, until 7 AM PST this morning.
Small Craft Advisory, from 7 AM this morning to 7 PM PST this
evening. Gale Warning, from 7 PM this evening to 4 PM PST
Friday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

A Gale Warning means winds of 34 to 47 knots are imminent or
occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

* WHAT...Southwest winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and

* WHEN...From 1 PM this afternoon to 1 AM EST Friday.

vessel for hazardous conditions.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Accumulating snowfall is expected inland and over higher terrain.

Locations: Gros Morne to Hawkes Bay. 

Potential snowfall: 20 to 30 cm, highest over elevated terrain. 

Time span: continuing until this evening. 

Remarks: Snow will accumulate steadily inland and over higher terrain while rain, or rain mixed with snow, is expected near the coast.

Snow may lead to adverse travel conditions, with slippery conditions in some locations, particularly over higher elevations.

Be prepared for winter driving conditions, keep a snow brush handy, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.
properties.stationOrArea: Gros Morne; Parson's Pond - Hawke's Bay

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
A prolonged period of snow continues, with total accumulations of 15 to 25 cm expected by Friday evening.

Snow will continue through Friday before beginning to taper off Friday evening.

Travel will likely be challenging. Visibility will likely be reduced at times.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Winds gusting up to 90 km/h are expected.

Southerly winds will continue to increase through the morning and remain strong through the day, accompanied by widespread blowing snow and reduced visibility.

These winds will gradually begin to diminish this evening, although they will continue to be gusty into Friday.

Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is occurring.

Where: East Vancouver Island - Nanoose Bay to Fanny Bay, Sunshine Coast.

When: Continuing through tonight.

What: Total rainfall amounts of 50 to 100 mm.

Remarks: A very robust frontal system continues to bring rain to the area tonight. The highest rainfall amounts are forecast for the communities between Qualicum Beach and Fanny Bay, with possible spillover to Powell River.

While rainfall rates have eased this evening for most areas, periods of moderate rain will likely redevelop overnight and end late Thursday morning.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: East Vancouver Island - Nanoose Bay to Fanny Bay; Sunshine Coast - Gibsons to Earls Cove; Sunshine Coast - Saltery Bay to Powell River

properties.title: Yellow warning · freezing rain warning
properties.rawText:
Patchy freezing rain will develop early this morning and end near noon.

Roads and walkways will likely become icy and slippery.

Be very careful if walking or driving.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NTstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NTStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: Ft. Liard Region including Nahanni Butte - Sambaa K'e; Ft. Simpson Region including Jean Marie River

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions with poor visibility in snow and blowing snow continues and will persist until this afternoon.

Snow will continue through Friday with 15 to 25 cm of new snow expected by Friday evening.

Southeast winds gusting up to 70 km/h will continue through today, resulting in reduced visibility in blowing snow. Winds will gradually begin to diminish this evening.

Travel will likely be hazardous.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

Blizzard warnings are issued when widespread poor visibility in blowing snow is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions with poor visibility in snow and blowing snow are expected to develop this morning.

Southerly winds will strengthen this morning, with gusts up to 90 km/h expected. Combined with falling snow, these strong winds will result in widespread blowing snow and poor visibility through the afternoon and evening.

Conditions will gradually improve later this evening, although intermittent blowing snow and reduced visibility can still be expected at times through the overnight hours.

Travel will likely be hazardous.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

HEBRIDES.
NORTH UIST AND SOUTH UIST WESTWARDS.
1. LIVE WEAPONS FIRINGS IN PROGRESS DAILY FROM 0700 TO 1900 UTC, 17 TO 20 NOV, IN AREA WITHIN 26 MILES OF 57-27N 008-16W.

ANY VESSELS INTENDING TO ENTER THE AREA SHOULD CONTACT HEBRIDES RANGE ON VHF CH16 OR TELEPHONE NUMBER +441870604449 / 4452 OR +447787328975 FOR ADVICE. MARITIME PATROL AIRCRAFT MAY BE IN OPERATION TO SUPPORT FIRINGS AND MARINERS ARE REQUESTED TO COMPLY WITH ANY INSTRUCTIONS GIVEN.
3. CANCEL THIS MSG 202000 UTC NOV 2026.

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning
properties.rawText:
Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 12 at 1:28PM EST until November 12 at 2:15PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ

At 127 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm was located over Wilmington,
moving east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail. This storm is
producing hail, with the hail accumulating in some areas in
northern New Castle County in Delaware.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to vehicles is possible. Wind damage to roofs,
siding, trees, and power lines is possible.

Locations impacted include...
Wilmington, Chester, Pennsville, Carneys Point, Folcroft, Elsmere,
Paulsboro, New Castle, Penns Grove, Woodstown, Swedesboro, Newport,
Arden, Stanton, Talleyville, Wilmington Manor, Beckett, Greenville,
Delaware Memorial Bridge, and Chester Township.

This includes the following highways...
New Jersey Turnpike between exits 1 and 2.
Interstate 95 in Pennsylvania between mile markers 0 and 10.
Interstate 95 in Delaware between mile markers 7 and 23.
Interstate 295 in New Jersey between mile markers 0 and 18.
Interstate 476 in Pennsylvania near mile marker 0.

A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 700 PM EST for northern
Delaware...southern New Jersey...and southeastern Pennsylvania.

Remain alert for a possible tornado! Tornadoes can develop quickly
from severe thunderstorms. If you spot a tornado go at once into the
basement or small central room in a sturdy structure.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm. Move
indoors immediately. Lightning is one of nature's leading killers.
Remember, if you can hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck
by lightning.
properties.stationOrArea: New Castle, DE; Gloucester, NJ; Salem, NJ; Delaware, PA

Tornado Warning issued November 12 at 1:25PM EST until November 12 at 1:45PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ

At 125 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located over Stanton, or near Wilmington, moving northeast at 25
mph.

HAZARD...Tornado and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

Locations impacted include...

and Edgemoor.

TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

properties.title: Tornado Warning
properties.rawText:
Tornado Warning issued November 12 at 1:14PM EST until November 12 at 2:00PM EST by NWS Upton NY

TOROKX

The National Weather Service in Upton NY has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Queens County in southeastern New York...

* Until 200 PM EST.

* At 113 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a tornado
was located over Rockaway Beach, moving northeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed.
Damage to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree
damage is likely.

* This dangerous storm will be near...
Rockaway Beach around 120 PM EST.
Kennedy Airport around 125 PM EST.

TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a basement or an interior room on the lowest
floor of a sturdy building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors, in a
mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to the closest substantial shelter
and protect yourself from flying debris.

Motorists should not take shelter under highway overpasses. If you
cannot safely drive away from the tornado, as a last resort, either
park your vehicle and stay put, or abandon your vehicle and lie down
in a low lying area and protect yourself from flying debris.

Heavy rainfall may hide this tornado. Do not wait to see or hear the
tornado. TAKE COVER NOW!

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Accumulating snowfall is expected inland and over higher terrain.

Locations: Gros Morne to Hawkes Bay. 

Potential snowfall: 20 to 30 cm, highest over elevated terrain. 

Time span: continuing until this evening. 

Remarks: Snow will accumulate steadily inland and over higher terrain while rain, or rain mixed with snow, is expected near the coast.

Snow may lead to adverse travel conditions, with slippery conditions in some locations, particularly over higher elevations.

Be prepared for winter driving conditions, keep a snow brush handy, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.
properties.stationOrArea: Gros Morne; Parson's Pond - Hawke's Bay

properties.title: Yellow advisory · fog advisory
properties.rawText:
Near-zero visibility in fog continues near Lloydminster. The fog is expected to persist into the afternoon.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ABstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #ABStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: City of Lloydminster; Co. of Two Hills near Two Hills and Brosseau; Co. of Two Hills near Myrnam and Derwent and 19 more areas

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Strong winds, with gusts of 90 to 100 km/h, are occurring or expected.

Southerly winds will continue to increase through the morning and remain strong throughout the day, accompanied by blizzard conditions.

Winds will weaken this evening, with some gusty winds continuing into Friday.

Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Severe wind gusts of 90 to 100 km/h are expected in Arctic Bay near noon today. 

Visibilities will also be reduced in falling snow to near blizzard condition. This warning may be upgraded to a blizzard warning if visibilities are poor. 

Winds should ease later this afternoon.

Driving conditions will likely be difficult. Some property damage is possible.

Secure loose objects. If outside, protect yourself from flying or falling debris.

Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is occurring.

Where: East Vancouver Island - Nanoose Bay to Fanny Bay, Sunshine Coast.

When: Now until early this afternoon.

What: Total rainfall amounts of 50 to 100 mm.

Remarks: A strong frontal system over the area will weaken today. Rain will continue to ease as the front weakens.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: East Vancouver Island - Nanoose Bay to Fanny Bay; Sunshine Coast - Gibsons to Earls Cove; Sunshine Coast - Saltery Bay to Powell River

properties.title: Yellow warning · freezing rain warning
properties.rawText:
Patchy freezing rain will end early this afternoon.

Roads and walkways will likely become icy and slippery.

Be very careful if walking or driving.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NTstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NTStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: Ft. Simpson Region including Jean Marie River

properties.title: Orange warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Very heavy rain is occurring.

Where: West and Inland Vancouver Island.

When: Now until early this afternoon.

What: Total rainfall amounts of 150 to 250 mm.

Remarks: A strong frontal system over the area will weaken today. Rain will continue to ease as the front weakens.

A weaker weather system will bring more rain tonight and Friday.

Localized flooding is likely. Some roads may become impassable. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Stay away from rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: West Vancouver Island; Inland Vancouver Island

Gale Warning issued November 12 at 1:18PM PST until November 13 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR

* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, seas 8 to 13 ft at 15
seconds and south winds 20 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt. For
the Gale Warning, seas 16 to 21 ft at 21 seconds and south winds
25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 45 kt expected. For the Hazardous
Seas Warning, very steep and hazardous seas 19 to 24 ft at 20
seconds and south winds 20 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt
expected.

* WHERE...Coastal waters from Cape Shoalwater WA to Cape Falcon
OR out 10 NM.

* WHEN...Small Craft Advisory, until 1 AM PST Friday. Gale
Warning, from 1 AM to 7 PM PST Friday. Hazardous Seas Warning,
from 7 PM Friday to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

A Gale Warning means winds of 34 to 47 knots are imminent or
occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

properties.title: Storm Warning
properties.rawText:
Storm Warning issued November 12 at 12:48PM PST until November 13 at 9:00AM PST by NWS Medford OR

* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, south winds 20 to 30 kt
with gusts up to 35 kt and seas 12 to 15 ft at 14 seconds. For
the Storm Warning, south winds 30 to 40 kt with gusts up to 60
kt and seas 14 to 19 ft at 14 seconds expected. For the Gale
Warning, south winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 45 kt and seas
18 to 25 ft at 14 seconds expected.

* WHERE...All area waters.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the Storm Warning, from 4 PM this afternoon to
9 AM PST Friday. For the Gale Warning, from 9 AM to 4 PM PST
Friday.

* IMPACTS...Very strong winds and very steep seas could capsize
or damage vessels. Visibilities will be significantly reduced.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Very steep, hazardous seas could reach 25
to 30 feet late Friday into Saturday as a heavy long period
swell continues to build in. Please stay tuned for updates on
this high impact weather pattern.

* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks

Mariners should remain in port, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for very strong winds and very steep and hazardous seas.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 12 at 11:41AM MST until November 17 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1140 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue
with flow peaking at 3000 cfs.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Yellow advisory · fog advisory
properties.rawText:
Near-zero visibility in fog is expected.

What:
Areas of dense fog with near-zero visibility.

When:
Now until late Friday morning.

Where:
East Kootenay - south including Cranbrook.

Additional information:
Conditions are favourable for the development of dense fog across parts of the Kootenays tonight. Dense fog is expected to lift or become patchy late Friday morning and may re-develop Friday evening.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Be prepared for areas of near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach your destination.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Severe wind gusts of 90 to 110 km/h are occurring in Arctic Bay. 

Visibilities could be reduced in falling snow. This warning may be upgraded to a blizzard warning if visibilities are poor. 

Winds should ease later this evening.

Driving conditions will likely be difficult. Some property damage is possible.

Secure loose objects. If outside, protect yourself from flying or falling debris.

Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Strong winds, with gusts up to 90 km/h, are possible.

These strong southerly winds, accompanied by blizzard conditions, may occur this evening before weakening.

Some gusty winds, with blowing snow, are expected on Friday.

Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are expected.

Where: Exposed coastal sections.

When: Tonight.

What: Southeast winds 80 gusting to 100 km/h.

Additional information:
An approaching frontal system will bring strong and gusty southeast  winds to the exposed coastal sections of West Vancouver Island. Southeast winds 80 gusting to 100 km/h will develop early this evening and will ease overnight.

Local utility outages are possible. Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Parks and forests will likely sustain some damage.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is expected.

Where: West and Inland Vancouver Island.

When: From this evening to late Friday afternoon.

What: Rainfall amounts of 50 to 100 mm except possibly exceeding 120 mm locally.

Remarks: A Pacific storm will approach Vancouver Island tonight bringing more rain to these regions. The heavy rain will begin this evening and will ease late Friday afternoon. Rainfall amounts of 50 to 100 mm, possibly exceeding 120 mm locally, are expected by Friday evening. 

The highest rainfall amounts are anticipated near Zeballos and Tahsis and over the northern sections of Inland Vancouver Island, including Gold River.

Another weather system will bring more rain this weekend.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Local utility outages are possible. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: West Vancouver Island; Inland Vancouver Island

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions with poor visibility in snow and blowing snow are occurring or expected.

Strong southerly winds, with gusts up to 90 km/h, combined with falling snow, will result in blowing snow and poor visibility this evening.

Conditions will gradually improve later this evening, although intermittent blowing snow and reduced visibility can be expected into Friday morning.

Travel will likely be hazardous.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

TO AVOID THE AREA.

PLANNING.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
The first notable snowfall of the season is expected  for inland areas and over higher terrain.

Locations: parts of mainland Nova Scotia and Cape Breton.

Potential snowfall: possibly reaching 5 cm.

Time span: Friday morning until Friday afternoon.

Remarks: A mix of snow and rain is forecast to begin Friday morning with some inland areas of Nova Scotia accumulating possibly up to 5 cm of snowfall by Friday afternoon. Coastal areas will see precipitation fall mainly as rain. 

Snow accumulation may make travel slow or hazardous. Roads and walkways could become slippery and difficult to navigate. 

Consider adjusting travel plans to avoid the most hazardous conditions.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NSstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NSStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Strong winds, with gusts up to 90 km/h, are possible.

These strong southerly winds, accompanied by blizzard conditions, may occur this evening before weakening.

Some gusty winds, with blowing snow, are expected on Friday.

Disruptions to services and travel are possible. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · freezing rain warning
properties.rawText:
Freezing rain mixing with snow this evening is expected to continue. 
Conditions should improve after midnight.

Icy surfaces could be difficult to detect. There is risk of injury due to slips and falls.

Freezing rain warnings are issued when rain falling in sub-zero temperatures is expected to create ice build-up.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions with poor visibility in snow and blowing snow are occurring or expected.

Strong southerly winds, with gusts up to 90 km/h, combined with falling snow, will result in blowing snow and poor visibility this evening.

Conditions will gradually improve later this evening, although intermittent blowing snow and reduced visibility can be expected into Friday morning.

Travel will likely be hazardous.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
The first notable snowfall of the season is expected  for inland areas and over higher terrain.

Locations: parts of mainland Nova Scotia and Cape Breton.

Potential snowfall: possibly reaching 5 cm.

Time span: this morning until this afternoon.

Remarks: A mix of snow and rain is forecast today with some inland areas of Nova Scotia accumulating possibly up to 5 cm of snowfall by this afternoon. Coastal areas will see precipitation fall mainly as rain. There is also a slight risk of freezing rain inland this morning.

Snow and ice accumulation may make travel slow or hazardous. Roads and walkways could become slippery and difficult to navigate. 

Consider adjusting travel plans to avoid the most hazardous conditions.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NSstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NSStorm.

properties.title: coastal flooding statement
properties.rawText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels are expected with enhanced wave activity and strong winds at times.
 
Hazard: Possible coastal flooding due to storm surge. Water levels will likely exceed highest astronomical tide.
 
When: Today and potentially into the weekend. Peak water levels will be observed during 10AM-12PM local time.
 
Where:  Low-lying and exposed coastal sections of Metro Vancouver and Musqueam First Nation including Boundary Bay to Semiahmoo Bay

Discussion:
A series of Pacific low-pressure systems will move across the region from now into the weekend and coincide with a period of high tides. High tides are likely to surpass predicted levels due to storm surge enhancement. East to Southeasterly winds gusting to 60-80km/h from now into the weekend are expected over exposed coastal sections at times. Moderate to potentially strong winds accompanying these systems can also cause enhanced wave action and swells in some areas.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Gale Warning
properties.rawText:
Gale Warning issued November 13 at 11:27AM PST until November 13 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR

* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and very
steep and hazardous, chaotic seas building to 25 to 30 ft at
19 seconds this evening. Then, tonight into Saturday morning,
southwest winds 20 to 30 kt tonight with very steep and
hazardous seas 25 to 30 ft at 18 seconds. Saturday afternoon
and evening, south winds 35 to 45 kt with gusts 55 to 60 kt
and seas 19 to 25 ft at 16 seconds expected.

* WHERE...All the area.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, until 7 PM PST this evening. For
the Hazardous Seas Warning, from 7 PM this evening to 1 PM PST
Saturday. For the Storm Warning, from 1 PM Saturday to 1 AM
PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Very strong winds and very steep seas could capsize
or damage vessels. Visibilities will be significantly reduced.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Another strong front will move in late
Saturday and Saturday night with the potential for storm force
winds and very steep and hazardous seas. This front will be
followed by another round of very high westerly swell Sunday
into Monday. Please continue to monitor the forecast for
updates on this high impact weather pattern.

Mariners should remain in port, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for very strong winds and very steep and hazardous seas.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 13 at 10:51AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to remain just at Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to remain
steady around Minor Flood Stage into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Water surrounds homes and covers some
driveways in the Stone Island area near Enterprise in Volusia
County. Water enters yards and floods docks in the River Oaks
Estates subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 5.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue rising to 5.5 feet just after
midnight tonight. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 1130 AM EST.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Winter weather travel statement in effect.

What:
Localized snowfall amounts of 5 to 10 cm.
Reduced visibility in areas of heavier snow.

When:
This evening into Saturday morning.

Where:
Areas of higher terrain south of Georgian Bay.

Discussion:
Lake effect snow off Georgian Bay is expected to intensify this evening. Although snowfall amounts are not expected to be overly significant, impacts may be higher than normal as this may be the first snowfall of the season for portions of the region.

Motorists should expect hazardous winter driving conditions and adjust travel plans accordingly.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. Slow down driving in slippery conditions. Watch for taillights ahead and maintain a safe following distance.

For road conditions and other traveller information from the Ministry of Transportation, visit https://www.ontario.ca/511, https://x.com/511Ontario, or call 5-1-1.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
The first notable snowfall of the season is expected  for inland areas and over higher terrain.

Locations: parts of mainland Nova Scotia and Cape Breton.

Potential snowfall: possibly reaching 5 cm.

Time span: until this afternoon.

Remarks: A mix of snow and rain is forecast today with some inland areas of Nova Scotia accumulating possibly up to 5 cm of snowfall by this afternoon. Coastal areas will see precipitation fall mainly as rain.

Snow and ice accumulation may make travel slow or hazardous. Roads and walkways could become slippery and difficult to navigate. 

Consider adjusting travel plans to avoid the most hazardous conditions.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NSstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NSStorm.

A. ALL ACFT OPS WI THE 5NM RADIUS AREA(S) LISTED ABV, KNOWN AS THE INNER CORE(S), ARE PROHIBITED EXC FOR: APPROVED LAW ENFORCEMENT, MIL ACFT DIRECTLY SUPPORTING THE UNITED STATES SECRET SERVICE (USSS) AND THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, APPROVED AIR AMBULANCE FLIGHTS, AND REGULARLY SCHEDULED COMMERCIAL PAX AND ALL-CARGO CARRIERS OPR UNDER ONE OF THE FOLLOWING TSA-APPROVED STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAMS/PROC AND ARE ARR INTO AND/OR DEP FM 14 CFR PART 139 AP: ACFT OPR STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAM (AOSSP), FULL ALL-CARGO ACFT OPR STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAM (FACAOSSP), MODEL SECURITY PROGRAM (MSP), TWELVE FIVE STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAM ALL CARGO (TFSSP-ALL CARGO), OR ALL-CARGO INTERNATIONAL SECURITY PROC (ACISP). ALL EMERGENCY/LIFE SAVING FLT (MEDICAL/LAW ENFORCEMENT/FIREFIGHTING) OPS MUST COORDINATE WITH ATC PRIOR TO THEIR DEP AT 866-598-9524 TO AVOID POTENTIAL DELAYS.
B. IFR AIRCRAFT ARR INTO AND / OR DEP FM JOINT
BASE ANDREWS (KADW)ARE AUTHORIZED TO OPERATE IN
THE TFR.
C. CFR PART 91 AND PART 135 AIRCRAFT OPERATORS ARR INTO AND/OR DEP FM WASHINGTON REAGAN NATIONAL AIRPORT (KDCA) OPERATING UNDER THE TRANSPORTATION SECURITY ADMINISTRATION DCA ACCESS STANDARD SECURITY PROGRAM (DASSP) ARE AUTHORIZED TO OPERATE IN THE TFR.
D. ALL WAIVERS TO FDC NOTAM 4/2565 AND 14 CFR PART 93 WASHINGTON DC SFRA/FRZ ARE TEMPORARILY SUSPENDED IN THE 5NM RING DURING THE TIME OF THIS NOTAM EXCEPT FOR WAIVERS BEGINNING WITH ELO, GOV, SPO, DAS, LEA, UFR AND LFG.
E. THE FOLLOWING OPS ARE NOT AUTH WI THIS TFR: FLT TRAINING, PRACTICE INSTRUMENT APCH, AEROBATIC FLT, GLIDER OPS, PARACHUTE OPS, ULTRALIGHT, HANG GLIDING, BALLOON OPS, AGRICULTURE/CROP DUSTING, ANIMAL POPULATION CTL FLT OPS, BANNER TOWING OPS, SIGHTSEEING OPS, MAINTENANCE TEST FLIGHTS, MODEL ACFT OPS, MODEL ROCKETRY, UNMANNED ACFT SYSTEMS (UAS), AND UTILITY AND PIPELINE SURVEY OPS.
F. UAS OPR WHO DO NOT COMPLY WITH APPLICABLE AIRSPACE RESTRICTIONS ARE WARNED THAT PURSUANT TO 10 U.S.C. SECTION 130I AND 6 U.S.C. SECTION 124N, THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE (DOD), THE DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY (DHS) OR THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE (DOJ) MAY TAKE SECURITY ACTION THAT RESULTS IN THE INTERFERENCE, DISRUPTION, SEIZURE, DAMAGING, OR DESTRUCTION OF UNMANNED ACFT DEEMED TO POSE A CREDIBLE SAFETY OR SECURITY THREAT TO PROTECTED PERSONNEL, FAC, OR ASSETS.
G. THE SYSTEM OPERATIONS SUPPORT CENTER (SOSC), IS THE COORDINATION FACILITY FOR GOVERNMENT AGENCIES AND IS AVAILABLE DAILY FROM 0700-2300 EASTERN, PHONE 202-267-8276 FOR COORDINATION.
H. THE FAA RECOMMENDS THAT ALL AIRCRAFT OPERATORS CHECK NOTAMS FREQUENTLY FOR POSSIBLE CHANGES TO THIS TFR PRIOR TO OPERATIONS WITHIN THIS REGION. OPERATORS MAY REVIEW THE TFR DETAILS ON THE INTERNET AT HTTPS://TFR.FAA.GOV/ OR HTTPS://WWW.1800WXBRIEF.COM. IF QUESTIONS REMAIN, CONTACT FLIGHT SERVICE AT 800-992-7433.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 13 at 2:53PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA

A large west to northwesterly swell is expected to produce
breaking waves at the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances
on Saturday. These conditions have a history of capsizing vessels
of various sizes resulting in serious injury or death, even to
the most experienced mariners. Mariners are urged to stay clear of
these harbor entrances. For more information, contact the local
harbor patrol or coast guard station...and continue to monitor
NOAA Weather Radio for the latest weather information..

ft at 14 to 15 seconds and south winds 30 to 40 kt with gusts
up to 55 kt expected.

* WHERE...Outer Coastal Waters from Cape Shoalwater to Florence
10 to 60 NM offshore.

* WHEN...Gale Warning, until 7 PM PST this evening. Hazardous
Seas Warning, from 7 PM this evening to 1 PM PST Saturday.
Storm Warning, from 1 PM Saturday to 4 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Very strong winds will cause hazardous seas which
could capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

A Storm Warning means winds of 48 to 63 knots are imminent or
occurring. Recreational boaters should remain in port, or take
shelter until winds and waves subside. Commercial vessels should
prepare for very strong winds and dangerous sea conditions, and
consider remaining in port or taking shelter in port until winds
and waves subside.

properties.title: special weather statement

What:
Localized snowfall amounts of 5 to 10 cm.
Reduced visibility in areas of heavier snow.

When:
This evening into Saturday morning.

Where:
Areas of higher terrain south of Georgian Bay.

Discussion:
Lake effect rain and snow showers off Georgian Bay are expected to intensify this evening and change to all snow over areas of higher terrain. 

Although snowfall amounts are not expected to be overly significant, impacts may be higher than normal as this may be the first snowfall of the season for portions of the region.

Motorists should expect hazardous winter driving conditions and adjust travel plans accordingly.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. Slow down driving in slippery conditions. Watch for taillights ahead and maintain a safe following distance.

properties.title: coastal flooding statement
properties.rawText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels are expected with enhanced wave activity and strong winds at times.
 
Hazard: Possible coastal flooding due to storm surge. Water levels will likely exceed highest astronomical tide.
 
When: Now and into the weekend. Peak water levels will be observed during 11am-2PM local time.
 
Where:  Low-lying and exposed coastal sections of the Southern Gulf Islands, Saanich Inlet, Swartz Bay to Cordova Bay, Cordova Bay to East Sooke
 
Discussion:
A series of Pacific low-pressure systems are moving across the region and coinciding with a period of high tides. High tides are likely to surpass predicted levels due to storm surge enhancement. East to southeasterly winds gusting to 60-90km/h now into the weekend are expected over exposed coastal sections at times. Moderate to potentially strong winds accompanying these systems can also cause enhanced wave action and swells in some areas.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Prolonged blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility in blowing snow are expected.

What:
Near-zero visibility in blizzard conditions.

When:
This evening to Monday evening.

Where:
Dempster Highway near the Richardson Mountains.

Additional information:
A persistent ridge of high pressure over the Beaufort Sea and a low pressure system over the Gulf of Alaska are generating a strong pressure gradient across the Richardson Mountains beginning this evening and lasting until Monday evening.

Winds will rise to easterly 60 km/h gusting to 80 this evening then further increase to 80 km/h gusting to 110 overnight. Wind-swept snow and falling snow combined with the strong winds will result in blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility. Winds will subside to 50 km/h gusting to 80 through Sunday and Monday but blizzard conditions will remain.

Road closures are possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 14 at 1:38AM EST until November 14 at 2:00AM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC

For the following areas...
Waters from Cape Lookout  to Surf City NC from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Ocracoke Inlet to Cape Lookout NC from 20 to 60 NM...

At 137 AM EST, a strong thunderstorm was located 32 nm southeast of
14 Buoy, moving east at 35 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to nearly 50 knots and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.
Wind gusts to nearly 50 knots, small hail, high waves, dangerous
lightning, and heavy rain are possible with this storm.
properties.stationOrArea: Waters from Ocracoke Inlet to Cape Lookout NC from 20 to 60 NM; Waters from Cape Lookout  to Surf City NC from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Hazardous Seas Warning
properties.rawText:
Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 13 at 10:00PM PST until November 14 at 1:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR

* WHAT...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, very steep and
hazardous seas 22 to 27 ft at 18 seconds and south winds 25 to
35 kt with gusts up to 40 kt. For the Storm Warning, seas 18
to 21 ft at 15 seconds and south winds 35 to 45 kt with gusts
up to 55 kt expected.

* WHERE...Outer Coastal Waters from Cape Shoalwater to Florence
10 to 60 NM offshore.

* WHEN...Hazardous Seas Warning, until 1 PM PST Saturday. Storm
Warning, from 1 PM Saturday to 4 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Very strong winds will cause hazardous seas which
could capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

A Storm Warning means winds of 48 to 63 knots are imminent or
occurring. Recreational boaters should remain in port, or take
shelter until winds and waves subside. Commercial vessels should
prepare for very strong winds and dangerous sea conditions, and
consider remaining in port or taking shelter in port until winds
and waves subside.
properties.stationOrArea: Waters from Cape Shoalwater WA to Cape Falcon OR from 10 to 60 nm; Waters from Cape Falcon to Cape Foulweather OR from 10 to 60 nm; Waters from Cape Foulweather to Florence OR from 10 to 60 nm

properties.title: Hazardous Seas Warning
properties.rawText:
Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 13 at 10:00PM PST until November 14 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR

* WHAT...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, very steep and
hazardous seas 22 to 27 ft at 19 seconds and south winds 25 to
35 kt with gusts up to 40 kt expected. For the Storm Watch,
seas 14 to 19 ft at 16 seconds and south winds 30 to 40 kt
with gusts up to 50 kt possible.

* WHERE...Inner Coastal Waters from Cape Shoalwater to Florence
out 10 NM.

* WHEN...Hazardous Seas Warning, until 4 PM PST Saturday. Storm
Watch, from Saturday afternoon through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Very strong winds will cause hazardous seas which
could capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

A Storm Watch is issued when the risk of storm force winds of
48 to 63 knots has significantly increased, but the specific
timing and/or location is still uncertain.  It is intended to
provide additional lead time for mariners who may wish to
consider altering their plans.

vessel for very strong winds and very steep and hazardous seas.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 13 at 7:24PM MST until November 17 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 724 PM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking at 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream  also indicated a stage of 9.93 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:06PM CST until November 17 at 1:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From Saturday evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CST Friday the stage was 10.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
Saturday evening to a crest of 15.0 feet early Sunday afternoon.
It will then fall below flood stage late Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Winter weather travel statement in effect.

What:
Localized snowfall amounts of 5 to 10 cm.
Reduced visibility in areas of heavier snow.

When:
Tonight into Saturday morning.

Where:
Areas of higher terrain south of Georgian Bay.

Discussion:
Lake effect rain and snow showers off Georgian Bay are expected to intensify and change to all snow over areas of higher terrain. 

Although snowfall amounts are not expected to be overly significant, impacts may be higher than normal as this may be the first snowfall of the season for portions of the region.

Motorists should expect hazardous winter driving conditions and adjust travel plans accordingly.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. Slow down driving in slippery conditions. Watch for taillights ahead and maintain a safe following distance.

For road conditions and other traveller information from the Ministry of Transportation, visit https://www.ontario.ca/511, https://x.com/511Ontario, or call 5-1-1.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 14 at 6:40AM MST until November 14 at 9:45AM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Kane County in southern Utah...
Southeastern Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 945 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is
occurring. National Park officials reported all area washes and
streams are running high and fast. The river gauge on the North
Fork of the Virgin River continues to increase, currently near 1000
cfs.  Similarly river gauges on the main stem of the Virgin River
upstream of Quail Creek show flows increasing rapidly.  Gould Wash
in Hurricane is running high.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 636 AM MST, local law enforcement reported heavy rain in the
warned area. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Zion National Park, Hurricane, La Verkin, Apple Valley,
Toquerville, Leeds, Virgin, Springdale, Rockville and Pintura.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.
